replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

- Automated abuse of a reachable endpoint: design has "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download" with "Invoice ids are sequential numbers" — already covered by listed threats 3 (bulk download DoS) and 4 (enumeration).
- Staff/admin/support screens showing other people's content: design states no such screen (only the customer download route) — not applicable.
- Delete/moderate/refund/role-change actions with no record: no such action in design; the only action is download, and the design records nothing about it — download accountability is **not covered** (listed threats cover access control, DoS, enumeration, not attribution of a leak).
- Personal/financial documents that browsers, proxies or CDNs could store: design states the PDF "contains the customer name, billing address and the last four digits of the card" served over a plain GET download URL — **not covered**.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, exports, emails, headers: design does not state any user-supplied text field or export; name/address are stated as PDF contents only — not applicable.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-04",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["invoice download endpoint", "PDF renderer", "customer web session"],
    "dataStores": ["invoice records"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["customer browser to web app"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [

      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Invoice PDFs with billing address and card last four left cacheable by browsers and shared proxies",
      "scenario": "The design serves invoice PDFs from a plain GET URL and says nothing about cache controls. The response holding the customer name, billing address and card last four can be retained by the browser disk cache, a corporate proxy or a CDN. Someone using the same shared or kiosk machine, or anyone able to query the intermediate cache, retrieves the stored PDF after the customer logs out, with no session and no access to the application at all.",
      "component": "/invoices/{invoiceId}/download response",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download." },
        { "quote": "The PDF contains the customer name, billing address and the last four digits of the card." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-525"],
      "plainLanguage": "Invoice PDFs with addresses and card digits can be saved by browsers or company proxies and read later by someone else on that machine or network.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Mark invoice PDF downloads non-cacheable",
        "given": "an authenticated customer requests /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "when": "the server returns the PDF containing name, billing address and card last four",
        "then": "the response sets Cache-Control: no-store (and private, no-cache) and Pragma: no-cache so browsers, shared proxies and CDNs do not retain a copy"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No download audit record, so an invoice data leak cannot be attributed or scoped",
      "scenario": "The design defines the download action but records nothing about it. If an attacker walks the sequential id range and pulls PDFs containing names, billing addresses and card last four, the team cannot tell which invoices were retrieved, which customers to notify, or whether a download came from the legitimate customer or a hijacked session. A customer or insider can also deny having downloaded a given invoice, and sustained scraping goes unnoticed because no download events exist to review or alert on.",
      "component": "invoice download endpoint (no audit log)",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers download invoices as PDFs from /invoices/{invoiceId}/download. Invoice ids are sequential numbers." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing is recorded when an invoice PDF is downloaded, so after a leak nobody can say which invoices were taken or by whom.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Log invoice download events",
        "given": "any request to /invoices/{invoiceId}/download",
        "when": "the server serves or denies the PDF",
        "then": "an audit record is written with timestamp, invoice id, requesting account id, source IP and outcome, retained for incident investigation and usable for high-volume download alerting"
      }
    }
  ]
}
